findings.reason: §9 should cite the existing implementations and collapse to landed, which removes the largest block of apparent remaining work.
findings.text: §9 ("One self-describing exemplar in-repo", the round-trip parity test at §9 line 253, and "Ship a single canonical authoring prompt") states as recommendations three mechanisms already in the tree: `docs/_exemplar-plan.html`, the round-trip parity test in `tests/test_schema.py` (the resolved `f-apa-roundtrip` followup records it landing as `cf5fb2b`), and the skill-level pointer at `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:34` / `skills/reckon-edit/SKILL.md:28` — the design section cites none of them and no section is marked landed, so a builder reading §9 would re-implement existing machinery

findings.reason: if the existing merge already covers a lone writer, the proposed flag is surface without behaviour; the section must extend the owner or drop the proposal.
findings.text: §9 proposes "a clearly-labelled force/merge for the lone-writer case so a transient version mismatch never blocks progress" without saying why the existing merge machinery (`merge_comment_collections`, `reckon/_plan_html.py:1077`, and the three-way landing merge at `reckon/_plan_html.py:1214`) cannot serve the lone-writer case, nor whether the escape hatch is a new CLI/MCP flag or a reuse of the existing merge

findings.reason: a parallel archival scheme fragments the cumulative record the owner exists to keep single; §6 must extend or cite the owner, not define a second one.
findings.text: §6 ("Per-stage archival. On a phase transition, write a NEW file under `docs/archive/<slug>-<phase>.html`") forks the archival owner `docs/AGENTS.md` §"Typed archives and cumulative evidence", which specifies one cumulative `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html` and states "Do not create a landed file per section, commit, or test wave … A phase transition does not justify another file" (`docs/AGENTS.md:52`); the proposed `docs/archive/` path exists in neither the owner nor the repo, and §4's collapse template repeats the scheme with a per-section link (`archive/SLUG-12-5-landed.html`, plan line 170)

findings.reason: the section adds MCP surface beside an existing owner without retiring the duplicate op names, so the plan must name what it removes or why nothing can be.
findings.text: §10 proposes "add_milestone/update_milestone" MCP ops that duplicate the existing typed-resource path (`edit_plan` with `doc_type="milestone"`, owner `reckon/mcp.py:1236`; the resolved `c-20261003T131057119940` comment records that those op names "were never needed"), and §9 (line 262) adds a force/merge escape hatch; neither section names what it retires or merges

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the design's central move is one file that hides parse, render, MCP and the version check behind a single HTML contract; the reframe consolidates surface rather than spreading it.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §6 re-implements archival as per-phase files under `docs/archive/<slug>-<phase>.html`, forking the archival owner `docs/AGENTS.md` which specifies one cumulative `docs/evidence/archive/<slug>-landed.html` and forbids a landed file per phase.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1470, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §9 adds a force/merge escape hatch and §10 adds `add_milestone`/`update_milestone` ops, and neither section names what it retires or merges.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §9 presents the in-repo exemplar, the render/parse round-trip test and the canonical authoring prompt as forward recommendations, while `docs/_exemplar-plan.html` (cited by `skills/reckon-create/SKILL.md:34`) and the round-trip parity test in `tests/test_schema.py` already exist; §9 cites neither.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §9's proposed force/merge escape hatch adds a thin layer over the existing version check and three-way merge machinery without stating why that machinery cannot serve the lone-writer case.
